intro: Three experiments on rotating systems. Race shapes down a ramp and watch where the energy goes; spin a student on a stool and pull the dumbbells in; launch a satellite and watch its kinetic and potential energy trade places while the total stays fixed.
howItWorks:
• Rolling without slipping: v = r ω, so kinetic energy is ½ m v² + ½ I ω² = ½ (1 + β) m v² when I = β m r². Hoop β = 1, solid disk ½, solid sphere ⅖ (given in questions, never memorized). Static friction makes it roll and does no work on it.
  • From energy, m g h = ½ (1 + β) m v², so v = √(2 g h / (1 + β)). Mass and radius cancel; only the shape (β) matters. The share of kinetic energy that is rotational is β / (1 + β).
  • Angular momentum L = I ω is conserved when no net external torque acts on the system. Pulling mass inward lowers I, so ω rises; K = L² / 2I rises too, paid for by the work the arms do.
  • Orbits: gravity on a small satellite points at the planet's center, so it exerts no torque about it: L is conserved. With U = −G M m / r (zero at infinity), E = K + U is conserved. On a circle, K, U and the speed √(G M / r) are constant; on an ellipse, K and U trade off, and the satellite is fastest when closest.

g = 9.8 m/s². Numbers count within 2%.
